questions.question: The classroom clock reads 10:15 a.m. when silent reading starts. It reads 10:40 a.m. when silent reading ends. How long did silent reading last?
questions.explain: Both times are in the same hour, so count on from 15 to 40 on the clock face: 40 − 15 = 25 minutes. The trap is adding the two numbers (15 + 40 = 55) — elapsed time is always the jump between the times, not their sum.

questions.question: How many minutes are there in 3 hours?
questions.explain: One hour is 60 minutes, so 3 hours = 3 × 60 = 180 minutes. The trap is treating time like money or place value and using 100 minutes per hour (3 × 100 = 300) — the clock counts in 60s, not 10s.

questions.question: Nadia's swim lesson at the community centre runs from 9:30 a.m. to 11:00 a.m. How long is the lesson?
questions.explain: Jump on a time line: 9:30 → 10:30 is 1 hour, then 10:30 → 11:00 is 30 more minutes, so 1 hour 30 minutes. The trap is subtracting like base-ten digits (11.00 − 9.30 = 1.70), which is not a real time amount because 70 minutes is more than an hour.

questions.question: Leo's school bus ride takes 45 minutes. He arrives at school at 8:20 a.m. What time does the bus pick him up?
questions.explain: To find a start time, jump backwards: 8:20 back 20 minutes is 8:00, then 25 more minutes back is 7:35 a.m. Two traps here — adding the 45 minutes instead of subtracting (9:05), and flipping the minutes when you cannot subtract (20 − 45 becomes 45 − 20, giving 7:25).

questions.question: Ava practises piano for 20 minutes every day for 3 weeks. How much time is that in total?
questions.explain: First convert weeks to days: 3 × 7 = 21 days, so 21 × 20 = 420 minutes, and 420 ÷ 60 = 7 hours. The traps are forgetting the week-to-day step (only 7 days gives 2 h 20 min) and reading 420 minutes as 4 h 20 min instead of dividing by 60.

questions.question: Amrit's spelling test started at 1:12 p.m. The teacher gave the class 40 minutes, but Amrit put his pencil down 7 minutes before the time was up. How long did Amrit work on the test?
questions.explain: Finishing early means the working time is shorter than the time allowed: 40 − 7 = 33 minutes (1:12 to 1:45). The trap is adding the 7 minutes (47) or reporting the finishing time's minutes (52) instead of the length of the jump.

questions.question: Owen's hockey practice runs from 6:50 p.m. to 8:15 p.m. His friend Sam's practice runs from 7:05 p.m. to 8:20 p.m. How much longer is Owen's practice than Sam's?
questions.explain: Find each length with time-line jumps first: Owen 6:50 → 8:15 is 85 minutes, Sam 7:05 → 8:20 is 75 minutes, so Owen's is 10 minutes longer. The trap is comparing only the start times (15 minutes) or only the end times (5 minutes) — you must compare the two durations.

questions.question: A BC Ferries sailing is scheduled to leave at 15:40 and the crossing takes 1 hour 35 minutes. On Saturday the ferry left 20 minutes late. Using 24-hour time, when did it arrive?
questions.explain: Do it in two steps: 15:40 + 20 min = 16:00 (the real departure), then 16:00 + 1 h 35 min = 17:35. The traps are ignoring the delay (17:15), counting the 20 minutes twice (17:55), and writing minutes past 60 instead of regrouping 60 minutes into 1 hour (16:95 is not a time).
